record.original_question: For a graph G on [n], let Q(G) be the family of independent vertex subsets and let s(G) be the size of a largest antichain in Q(G). Under what conditions on G do we have s(G) equal, or asymptotically close, to the size of the largest layer max_r |Q(G)^(r)|?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7. When do we have (almost) equality in ( 1) ? What conditions on G are sufficient to guarantee (almost) equality ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with vertex set [n] = {1, 2, ..., n}. Define Q(G) to be the family of all independent vertex subsets of G (i.e., subsets S ⊆ [n] containing no edge of G), partially ordered by inclusion. For each integer r ≥ 0, let Q(G)^(r) denote the r-th layer of Q(G), namely the collection of independent sets of size exactly r, and write L(G) = max_r |Q(G)^(r)| for the size of the largest layer. Let s(G) denote the maximum size of an antichain in Q(G) (a family of independent sets, no one of which is contained in another). It is well-known that s(G) ≥ L(G).

Determine structural conditions on the graph G under which equality s(G) = L(G) holds, and more generally conditions guaranteeing the asymptotic equality s(G) = (1 + o(1)) L(G) as n → ∞. In particular, characterize (or give broad sufficient conditions on) those graphs G for which the independence complex Q(G) has the Sperner property, or is asymptotically Sperner.
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of characterizing graphs G for which the largest antichain in the independence-set lattice equals (or is asymptotically equal to) the largest layer remains open. Partial results exist: Sperner's theorem handles the edgeless graph, and for paths the largest antichain is known to be of the same order as the largest layer. Work of Engel, Bohman, and others on G-independent Sperner problems gives partial answers, but no general characterization is known.

status_evidence.title: Sperner's problem for G-independent families
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Sperner-type questions for the family of independent sets of a graph G, providing partial results for specific graph classes such as paths.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are known for specific classes of graphs but no general characterization.

status_evidence.title: Sperner's problem for G-independent families (CPC)
status_evidence.snippet: For G the path of length n−1, the size of a maximal antichain in Q(G) is of the same order as the size of a largest layer of Q(G).
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic equality is established for paths, but the general problem remains open.
